title: Red Sea military escalation optionality around Bab el-Mandeb
net_new_delta: Reuters reports Saudi Arabia is preparing a Yemeni-led offensive intended to break Houthi control around Bab el-Mandeb. This materially raises event risk to Red Sea shipping, but the timing, execution, success and resulting shipping-flow effects remain unconfirmed.
assumptions_affected: Red Sea shipping disruption is a static background condition
Energy risk can be represented only through Hormuz/crude channels

evidence.finding: Saudi Arabia is preparing a Yemeni-led offensive, backed by Saudi air support and U.S. intelligence, aimed at breaking Houthi control of the Bab el-Mandeb area; timing remains tentative.

fact: A Reuters report exists describing preparations for an offensive around Bab el-Mandeb; the report does not establish that the operation has begun or succeeded.
model_inference: Create RED_SEA_ESCALATION_OPTIONALITY as an event-risk state; do not promote to realized shipping normalization or realized supply disruption without traffic/attack/flow evidence.
conflicts: An offensive could eventually reopen/normalize shipping, but its initiation could first increase attack and retaliation risk; direction of near-term market impact is therefore ambiguous.
next_decisive_check: Require confirmation that operations have begun, then check UKMTO/JMIC incident reports, Bab el-Mandeb vessel traffic/rerouting, freight/insurance repricing and physical energy flows before promoting the state.

oracle.finding: Red Sea risk now contains a two-sided transition state: prospective military action could ultimately improve passage security but can initially raise retaliation and shipping-disruption risk; model it separately from Hormuz and realized energy supply.

supermesh_x.finding: Route Reuters as preparation evidence only; require UKMTO/JMIC plus vessel-traffic and physical-flow confirmation for realized maritime or energy-state promotion, preserving source-role separation.
